2025:KER:77683

 IN THE HIGH COURT OF KERALA AT ERNAKULAM

 PRESENT

 THE HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN

 &

 THE HONOURABLE MRS. JUSTICE M.B. SNEHALATHA

FRIDAY, THE 17TH DAY OF OCTOBER 2025 / 25TH ASWINA, 1947

 MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND DECREE DATED 28.12.2021 IN

 OP NO.835 OF 2018 OF FAMILY COURT, KANNUR

APPELLANT/PETITIONER:

 SEBASTIAN JOSEPH M., AGED 48 YEARS
 S/O. JOSEPH, MANNARTHARA HOUSE,
 PULIKKURUMBA P.O, TALIPARAMBA TALUK,
 KANNUR DISTRICT, PIN-670 582.


 BY ADV.
 SHRI.P.U.SHAILAJAN


RESPONDENTS/RESPONDENTS:

 1 LIJA P.SEBASTIAN, AGED 46 YEARS
 D/O. SEBASTIAN, PAALATHADATHIL HOUSE,
 PERUMBADAVU P.O, TALIPARAMBA TALUK,
 KANNUR DISTRICT, PIN-670 581,
 NOW WORKING AT LITTLE FLOWER ENGLISH MEDIUM
 SCHOOL, KOTTOOR, SREEKANDAPURAM.

 2 JITHESH JOHN, AGED 30 YEARS
 S/O. JOHN, KOCHUPURACKAL HOUSE,
 CHEMBERI P.O, ERUVESSRI AMSOM DESOM,
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -2-


 TALIPARAMBA TALUK, KANNUR DISTRICT,
 PIN-670 632.


 BY ADVS.
 SRI.LIJIN THAMBAN
 SRI.G.S.KRISHNAN KARTHA
 SMT.AKSHARA K.V.


 THIS MATRIMONIAL APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD
ON 17.10.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE
FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -3-


 JUDGMENT
Devan Ramachandran, J.

The appellant filed OP No.835/2018 before

the learned Family Court, Kannur, seeking

divorce from the 1st respondent herein, namely

his wife, invoking the provisions of Section

10(x) of the Indian Divorce Act, 1869 ('Act',

for short).

2. The appellant alleges that his wife

has had an adulterous relationship with the 2 nd

respondent, as also with another person - who,

in fact, testified as PW2; and hence that he is

entitled to a decree for divorce on the ground

of adultery.

3. The learned Family Court took the

matter to trial and recorded the deposition of
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -4-


the appellant as PW1, as also that of PW2 and

PW3; while, the 1st respondent offered testimony

as RW1. The Court also marked Exts.A1 to A3

documents produced by the appellant, but did not

admit Ext.A4 series pen drives into evidence.

It, after evaluation of the evidence on record,

dismissed the Original Petition, finding the

allegations to be unproved.

4. We are constrained to record upfront

that this is a rather strange case where, the

appellant had summoned one of the alleged

adulterers as a witness on his side and examined

him as PW2, but without arraying him as a

respondent. After the said witness testified in

his favour, agreeing that he had had an

adulterous relationship with the 1st respondent

for four years, the appellant applied to bring
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -5-


him on array as a respondent, but this was

disallowed by the learned Family Court, which

order remains unimpeached.

6. The gravamen of the allegations of the

appellant is that his wife, the 1 st respondent

herein, is leading an immoral life with multiple

partners, namely Respondent No.2 and PW2. His

assertions are supported by his mother, namely

PW3, who testified to the effect that the 2nd

respondent has come to the matrimonial home of

the parties two or three times and that he and

the 1st respondent would spend their time in the

ancestral home, with her bedroom being locked

from outside.

7. However, the 1st respondent, as RW1,

vehemently controverted every imputation against

her; contra - alleging that she had been
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -6-


subjected to inhumane torture and abuse by her

husband and mother-in-law, namely PW1 and PW3;

and that she had, therefore, been constrained to

approach the Police through a complaint,

especially since a violent attempt was made by

them to oust her from the matrimonial home. She

added that, however, since the Police did not

'Act', she approached the Court of the Judicial

Magistrate of the First Class, Taliparamba, with

a complaint; and that it was after she did,

that the allegations of adultery came to be made

against her, such being mala fide and cruel.

8. As far as the testimony of the

appellant as PW1 is concerned, he deposed that

he is working in the Indian Military Service and

conceded that his wife had filed a complaint

against him on 09.07.2018 before the Police,
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -7-


alleging ill-treatment. He stated that, she

thereafter left the matrimonial home, to appear

before the Kudiyanmala Police Station, where he

and his parents were also present; and that she

told him that she had no interest in continuing

with their matrimonial life. He stated that he

was annoyed by this conduct of his wife; and

that, when he then made enquiries, it was

revealed that she had connections with the 2 nd

respondent - who was a frequent visitor to his

house - and that they were indulging in sexual

intercourse, after locking PW3 - his mother - in

her bedroom. He then went to the extent of

saying that, when he searched the house, he

found liquor bottles; and that when he

confronted his wife about this, she left his

house; further stating that he had reported all
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -8-


this to the Kudiyanmala Police Station, from

where the matter was referred to the Kannur

'Vanitha Cell'. He claimed that, when the Police

interrogated the 1st respondent, she confessed to

the adulterous relationship between herself and

the 2nd respondent, as also with the PW2; and

that they had a conversation thereafter, which

had been recorded by him and produced before the

Court as Exts.A4 series pen drives.

9. The learned Court, however, found that

Ext.A4 series cannot be admitted in evidence

because, they were not supported by the

statutory certification; and since PW1 could not

even say whose phone it was recorded in and how

it was then transferred to the pen drives.

10. At this time, we must digress to

notice that, pending this Appeal, the appellant
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -9-


moved IA No.1/2025 before us, seeking to produce

certain certificates purported to be under

 Sections 61 and 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya

Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA), with respect to the pen

drives in question. We, however, dismissed the

said application through our order on

12.08.2025, which is reproduced under:

This application is untenable and
 not maintainable because the documents
 sought to be produced are purported to be
 certificates prepared under Sections 61 
 and 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya
 Adhiniyam, 2023, with respect to a pen
 drive which had been denied as the
 evidence by the learned Trial Court
 because the relevant certificates qua the
 same had not been produced during
 evidence.

One fails to understand how the
 petitioner now seeks to produce
 certificates created after the evidence
 was over.

2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -10-


 That apart, the certificates do
 not even mention the date on which the
 information was transferred to the pen
 drive. Further, even the dates on which
 the transfer of the information from one
 device to another occurred, even more
 than once, have not been mentioned. We
 just cannot, therefore, understand what
 was the purport of the relief from the
 petitioner in this application. This
 application is, therefore, dismissed.

11. As we have said earlier, this is a

rather incredulous case where one of the alleged

adulterers testified in favour of the appellant,

as PW2, saying that he had sexual intercourse

with the 1st respondent multiple times for over

four years. Interestingly, he explained that he

had approached a "Dhyana Guru" and that he had

reformed himself, to come forward and state
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -11-


truth in Court. However, the learned Family

Court found from his evidence that he had

previous acquaintance with the appellant and

that he was asked to reach the Court as per the

instructions of the latter's learned counsel;

and then went on to hold that this proves the

"cunningness" of the petitioner (appellant

herein).

12. The afore findings of the learned

Family Court certainly are on terra firma

because, when the appellant says that he was

aware that PW2 was an adulterer, nothing

prevented him from making him a respondent; but,

on the contrary, what he did was to call him as

a witness on his side and to extract testimony

from him, which reads as a virtual confession.

The matter did not end there! As also seen
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -12-


earlier, after such testimony was recorded, an

application was made to arraign him as a

respondent, which the learned Family Court did

not accede to - in our view, correctly.

13. Coming to the alleged allegations of

adultery between the 1st respondent and

respondent No.2, there is not even a shred of

evidence available, as has also been correctly

found by the learned Family Court, to prove any

such.

14. As noticed earlier, it is the version

of PW3, the mother of the appellant, which is

impelled as a clinging one by the latter; and

she said that the 2nd respondent visited her

house occasionally, and that her bedroom would

be locked while the respondents indulged in

sexual activities in the ancestral home. How she
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -13-


saw such activity, while locked in her room, is

a real mystery left unexplained.

15. Incredulous as this may seem, the

evidence of PW1 then goes on to say that he

found liquor bottles in his home, insinuating

that the 1st respondent had consumed the same;

and that she had confessed about her adulterous

relationship with both PW2 and respondent No.2,

when she was confronted at the Police Station.

All these remain without any corroboration.

16. The afore being said, it is also

pertinent that the appellant had only invoked

 Section 10(x) of the 'Act', alleging that he was

treated cruelly. However, every allegation in

the Original Petition, as can be discerned from

its close reading, is hinged on the assertion

that the 1st respondent has lived an adulterous
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -14-


life with the 2nd respondent and PW2, without any

other instance of cruel behaviour.

17. However, contra-distinctly, RW1

testified that she was continuously attacked

physically by the appellant; and that she was

then forced to take employment in a private

school to take care of her children and herself.

She added that, in October 2017, the appellant

assaulted her brutally after reaching home in a

drunken state; and that she was driven out of

the home, thus being constrained to take shelter

by hiding herself in an old toilet of the

residential premises. She testified that she was

instilled with the fear of her life and that she

was threatened that she could not return unless

she brought additional gold and money. She

further testified that she had thus gone to the
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -15-


Police Station to file a petition.

18. We cannot comprehend how the plea of

cruelty could have been so casually used by the

appellant in such scenario, especially when

there is not even a whisper of any instance

cited by the appellant - apart from the

allegations of adultery against the 1st

respondent - to establish that he had been

treated with such, so as to cause a reasonable

apprehension in his mind that it would be

harmful or injurious for him to live with her.

This is the sine qua non for any application

under Section 10(x) of the 'Act', and when such

are completely missing and devoid from the

Original Petition, the learned Family Court

would have been even justified in dismissing the

Original Petition without trial, but it rightly
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -16-


chose not to do so and allowed the parties to

lead evidence, which again discloses only

uncorroborated and unproved allegations of

adultery and nothing else. Obviously, an

application under Section 10(x) of the 'Act'

becomes untenable.

19. Even disregarding the afore technical

impediment we have recorded, it is rendered

ineluctable that the allegations of adultery

against the 1st respondent have not been proved

at all - with the evidence of PW2 and PW3 being

totally unworthy and incapable of any

acceptance.

20. The assertion of the appellant, that

there are confessions by the 1st respondent, also

remains without any proof; and this, coupled

with the latter having made allegations against
 2025:KER:77683
MAT.APPEAL NO. 65 OF 2023

 -17-


him and his mother of ill-treating her, before

the Police Station and the learned Magistrate,

disentitles him to any relief, as has been

correctly done by the learned Family Court.

The summation of our findings and

observations above is inevitable that this

Appeal lacks merit; and we consequently, dismiss

it with costs to the 1st respondent.
Sd/-

DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN
 JUDGE


 Sd/-

M.B.SNEHALATHA
akv JUDGE
